candidate_additions: Explicit two-arm structure (mevalonate arm vs post-squalene sterol arm) with defined enzyme order
Erg28 reassigned a specific molecular role as non-catalytic scaffold binding Nsdhl/Msmo1 in the C4-demethylation complex, plus a feedback claim that Erg28 loss impairs SREBP-2 activation

Direct SRE promoter-binding evidence added for Erg28, Dhcr7, and distinctive gene Rdh11, sharpening the transcriptional-control mechanism from 'controls the pathway' to 'binds these specific promoters'
New distinctive gene Ddr2 introduced with a specific anti-steatotic AMPK/ACC mechanism in MASLD liver
Fads2 added as a regulator linking PUFA synthesis/lipogenesis to the lipid-homeostasis context
candidate_removed_or_weakened: Ldlr as the SREBP2-driven cholesterol-uptake arm of the circuit is dropped entirely from the candidate
Baseline's aging/senescence claim (mevalonate pathway overactivity drives hepatic cellular senescence via the ERRα/mitochondrial axis) is removed and not replaced with any aging-related claim
decision_relevant_differences: Baseline points a reader toward senescence/ERRα/mitochondrial dysfunction as the aging-relevant downstream consequence of this program; candidate offers no support for that and instead proposes an anti-steatotic Ddr2/AMPK-ACC axis as the MASLD-relevant context, a different follow-up hypothesis

Candidate's scaffold (not enzyme) role for Erg28, with a bidirectional Erg28-SREBP2 feedback claim, changes what kind of validation experiment (complex/structural vs enzymatic) would be prioritized for that gene
Candidate supplies specific SRE promoter-binding claims (Erg28, Dhcr7, Rdh11) giving more direct transcriptional mechanistic evidence than baseline's generic 'SREBP2 controls this gene set'
Dropping Ldlr means a reader using only the candidate loses the uptake-arm component of the transcriptional circuit that baseline described
assessment.rationale: Both annotations agree P21 is the mevalonate-to-cholesterol biosynthesis program under SCAP/Insig1/SREBP2 control with the same enzyme roster and the same MASLD-linked regulators (Dgat2, Mttp) — the central interpretation is preserved. The candidate meaningfully refines this with gene-specific mechanistic claims (Erg28 as scaffold with feedback to SREBP2, direct SRE sites for three genes) and extends the MASLD arm with a new gene (Ddr2) and regulator (Fads2). It also drops two baseline claims (Ldlr as uptake arm; senescence/ERRα/mitochondrial link in aging) without replacing them with an aging-relevant mechanism, which is a real narrowing of the disease-context narrative but does not alter the program's core enzymatic/regulatory identity. This pattern — retained core, added gene-function detail, one context-level mechanism reframed/removed — matches 'same_core_with_meaningful_refinement' rather than a material change to the program's central interpretation.
shared_core_conclusions: P21 is a near-complete transcriptional program for de novo mevalonate/cholesterol biosynthesis in hepatocytes, covering essentially the same enzyme set (Hmgcs1, Idi1, Mvk, Pmvk, Mvd, Fdps, Fdft1, Lss, Cyp51, Msmo1, Nsdhl, Hsd17b7, Tm7sf2, Sc5d, Dhcr7, Erg28)
Acss2 supplies acetyl-CoA as pathway carbon source and Acat2 esterifies cholesterol
Scap and Insig1 form the ER-anchored SREBP2 toggle that transcriptionally controls the whole enzyme set
Dgat2 and Mttp connect VLDL/triglyceride handling to the program in the MASLD disease context
